note:
MORODER — Munich 1977. "I Feel Love", Musicland Studios: Giorgio
Moroder and Pete Bellotte sequence a Moog Modular for the whole
rhythm track — the delay throwing every eighth into the gap —
and Donna Summer floats over the machine. The record dance music
dates its own mechanization from. TWO rows have wanted "eurodisco"
by name since their lineages were written — `synthpop` (Basildon
1981) and `electro` (New York 1982) — and `italodisco` below is
built on it directly. An ARTIST anchor, the synthsoul
precedent: the producer is the genre.

ITS OWN ARPEGGIO (2026-08-31): I Feel Love IS the octave pedal — this row's own comment already said "the arpeggiated octave" while the record had none.

LINEAGE: `phillysoul` (Philadelphia 1972) is the four-on-the-
floor and the string ceiling the sequencer replaced player by
player; `funk` the syncopated bass the Moog line abstracts;
`dusseldorfschool` is deliberately NOT here — Trans-Europe Express is
the same year, and this row's machine groove was built in
parallel, not inherited (the two records famously heard each
other AFTER the fact).

WHO SINGS: falsetto — Summer's held head-voice coo,
deliberately weightless against the machine.

CLOSEST, ANSWERED 2026-09-03 (the catalogue round, shift 3). The QA report's
`closest` column ranks each declared parent against every older row by a FEATURE
VECTOR — bpm, swing, major/minor, kit density, harmony kind, plan, nobass,
instrumental, family — and calls a parent sitting in the further half of that
ranking suspect. The vector has no term for the thing a child actually TAKES
from a parent, so an ancestor the record deliberately departs from ranks far by
construction, and the catalogue's trunk rows — funk, jazz, swing, ballad,
ambient, punk, drone, gregorian — rank far from nearly every leaf they grew.
THE PARENTS ON THIS ROW STAND. What the vector cannot see: `funk` is the BASS AND THE FOUR ON THE FLOOR that Munich sequenced, and the
vector reads a 1969 band against a 1977 machine. `dusseldorfschool` (1977) is
offered as nearer and is the same year: Moroder and Kraftwerk are contemporaries
who arrived at the sequencer separately, which is why `synthpop` declares BOTH of
them and neither declares the other.
label: Munich 1977
words: the Moog line, delayed into sixteenths
the voice, floating over the machine
the pad, one chord a bar
